title: The Ballad of Mulan
text:
Mulan sat at her loom, but instead of the click of the shuttle there were only her sighs. The night before, she had seen the army notices. The Khan was calling up troops, and the conscription lists, twelve scrolls of them, all carried her father's name. Her father had no grown son, and she had no older brother.

So she decided to go in his place. She bought a fine horse in the east market, a saddle in the west market, a bridle in the south and a long whip in the north. At dawn she left her parents, and by evening she was camped by the Yellow River, hearing not her father and mother calling her but the rushing of the water.

She served for years, through cold nights on the frontier and many battles. When the army returned victorious, the Son of Heaven offered her high office and rich rewards. Mulan asked only for a swift camel to carry her home.

Her parents came out to meet her, her older sister put on her finest makeup, her little brother sharpened a knife to kill a pig and a sheep for a feast. Mulan changed back into her old dress, did her hair before the mirror and went out to greet her comrades. They were astonished. In twelve years together they had never known she was a woman.
lesson: Love for family can call out courage nobody suspected. When the moment passes, the greatest reward may simply be coming home.
source: The Ballad of Mulan (Mulan Shi), anonymous, preserved in Guo Maoqian, Yuefu Shiji (12th century)
caveat: Mulan is a figure of legend and poetry, and there is no reliable evidence that she was a historical person.
